A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CostFilter-AD and contain 25 pages, including Appendices A–J. Their text, equations, tables and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original anomaly detection experiments on MVTec-AD, VisA, BTAD and MPDD, including method comparisons, ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments, with revised computational-cost figures and appendix results.

M1.justification: The cost-volume construction, filtering network, dual-stream attention, class-aware adaptor, losses and inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendix labels change from '+Ours' to '+UCF' without a documented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four datasets and retain the single-class, multi-class, template-type and full-shot evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including UniAD, GLAD, HVQ-Trans, AnomalDF and Dinomaly. Revised comparator scores do not introduce different comparison methods.

E3.justification: The stated splits, resolutions, template protocols, metrics and training settings remain unchanged. Batch size 1 is newly disclosed for existing efficiency measurements; v3 states no conflicting measurement batch size.

E4.justification: The component ablations, template compatibility study, full-shot/resolution analysis, failure cases and progressive-denoising examples are retained. Figures 9 and 11 retain the underlying distribution plots despite rendering and numerical-annotation changes.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-estimation procedures. The KDE plots continue to describe logit distributions.

E6.justification: Substantial numerical revisions affect Table 7 and appendix Tables 9–20. Table 7 changes module FLOPs from 207.8G to +26.0G for UniAD/HVQ-Trans, 261.3G to +32.7G for GLAD/AnomalDF, and 114.6G to +14.3G for Dinomaly. Table 10 changes Dinomaly plus the proposed method's mean MVTec-AD pixel AP from 68.9 to 75.6; Table 12 changes UniAD plus the method's Screw AUPRO from 60.0 to 95.0. Baseline scores and Figures 9/11 AUROC annotations also change. These are reported-value revisions; the PDFs do not establish reruns or procedural improvements.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and the mathematical definitions remain equivalent. No assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about matching-noise filtering, generic plug-in applicability and strong single-class and multi-class anomaly detection.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning matching noise, complementary templates and attention guidance remain unchanged. Section 4.5 retains the same limitations involving weak anomaly signals, input resolution and feature extraction.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 newly specifies that all efficiency measurements use batch size 1. The A100 GPU specification, training details, Appendix A implementation information and planned code/model release statement are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to anomaly detection and cost-volume filtering research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds the efficiency-measurement sentence and changes appendix table terminology from '+Ours' to '+UCF'. The section order and substantive explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: Appendix tables are restyled through changes to shading, spacing and headers. Figures 9 and 11 are re-rendered with adjusted panel proportions and labels, and page 9 text reflows. The figure/table inventory and ordering remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves reporting by disclosing the efficiency-test batch size and fixing demonstrable arithmetic inconsistencies: Table 10's Dinomaly mean pixel AP changes from 68.7 to 69.8, matching its retained category values. However, revised appendix results are not consistently propagated: Dinomaly plus the method has mean pixel AP 75.6 in Table 10 while Table 3 retains 68.9. These unresolved discrepancies limit the overall gain.
